name: Today's Report
headline: A soft jobs report did not bring mortgage rates down, and the East Bay has added almost no jobs this year.
teaser: Friday's jobs report was soft, and mortgage rates rose anyway. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fixed ended the week at 7.57% and the 15-year at 7.19%, and the 10-Year Treasury is higher again this morning, near 5.33%. A weak jobs report usually helps rates; this one did not get the memo.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Friday's jobs report was soft, and mortgage rates rose anyway. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fixed ended the week at 7.57% and the 15-year at 7.19%, and the 10-Year Treasury is higher again this morning, near 5.33%. A weak jobs report usually helps rates; this one did not get the memo.

Here, flat hiring is not new. The Oakland, Fremont and Berkeley metro division added only about 500 jobs from December to August, while the San Jose area added 14,700 (see the chart in Economy).

Locally, the five city ledger held at 664 for a third straight day, though the mix shifted: Union City rose to 60 and Fremont slipped to 238. The board wide table edged up to 2,688 from 2,687.

What this means for you: at 7.57%, the five city median list price of $1,070,000 with 20% down runs about $6,026 a month in principal and interest. Slower hiring can thin the buyer pool, so sellers should price for the buyers who are here today. Buyers with steady income have more leverage; ask for seller credits toward a rate buydown.

  • Board wide: 2,688 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 167 coming soon and 202 brand new.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Live ledger: 664 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 583 are on the market and 81 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 238 live, 187 active, 32 coming soon, 18 brand new and 1 back on market. The median on market list price is $1,249,495 at $777 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 31 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 173, Milpitas 106, Newark 87, Union City 60.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,070,000 at $675 a square foot. 276 homes are priced under a million, and 139 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Hiring has hit a wall. Employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, July was revised to a loss of 10,000, and 2026 is averaging 68,000 a month. The unemployment rate rose to 4.2%.

The chart's right panel is the local view: San Jose is still hiring, while the East Bay has gone sideways all year. Bond traders read the soft report and sold anyway, which is why mortgage rates went the wrong way on Friday.

images.alt: Two panel chart of payroll jobs, seasonally adjusted. Left, a line of the monthly change in U.S. payroll jobs in 2026: January +160,000, February minus 156,000, March +214,000, April +148,000, May +63,000, June +31,000, July minus 10,000, August +133,000 and September +29,000, against a 2026 average of +68,000 a month. Right, jobs added from December 2025 to August 2026: San Jose metro +1.26% (14,700 jobs), California +0.64% (114,700), United States +0.37% (583,000), and the Oakland, Fremont and Berkeley metro division +0.04% (about 500).
images.caption: U.S. hiring slowed to 29,000 in September and is averaging 68,000 a month this year. The Oakland, Fremont and Berkeley metro division has added about 500 jobs since December.
images.source: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Ford has had a rough ride. The stock closed Friday at $12.10, down 7.8% for 2026 while the S&P 500 is up 12.8%, and 31% below its May 29 high of $17.44. That peak was a battery storage rally: shares jumped 13% on May 13 after a bullish Morgan Stanley call on Ford Energy, and on May 18 Ford agreed to supply EDF with up to 20 GWh of grid storage starting in 2028.

September let the air out: a recall of 223,472 F-150s over fuel tank straps, a supplier problem that disrupted F-150 production at month end, and third quarter U.S. sales down 6.6%. Ford says the sales drop reflects the planned end of the Escape and Corsair, and that the supplier issue fits inside its $10 billion to $11 billion profit guidance. Ford is unchanged this morning at $12.10.

images.alt: Line chart of Ford Motor Co.'s closing share price from December 31, 2025 to October 2, 2026. It started the year at $13.12, fell to a low of $11.21 on March 30, jumped 45% in 12 sessions in a May battery storage rally to a high of $17.44 on May 29, then slid through September to $12.10 on October 2, down 7.8% for the year and 31% below the May high. Over the same span the S&P 500 rose 12.8% and GM fell 3.8%.
images.caption: Ford has given back its whole May battery storage rally and closed Friday 7.8% below where it started the year, while the S&P 500 is up 12.8%.
images.source: Source: Nasdaq closing prices for Ford and GM, CNBC for the S&P 500, Ford's Q3 2026 U.S. sales release, NHTSA recall 26V578.
